event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Healing Harvest Market

Hosted by Valley Vital Medicine
First Friday of Every Month | 3–6 PM
Location: Valley Vital Medicine, Fargo, ND
Website: https://valleyvitalmedicine.com

The Healing Harvest Market is a monthly community gathering focused on faith, health, and local nourishment. Each market features local farmers, artisans, and wellness-focused businesses offering clean food, handcrafted goods, and natural wellness resources.

This event is an opportunity for the community to come together, support small local producers, and learn more about healthy, intentional living. The market also highlights ways to support local families and individuals facing health challenges.

All are welcome to attend and connect with others who value community wellness, local agriculture, and meaningful living.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Catering to families with young skaters, this Saturday morning session offers discounted admission for families along with age-appropriate music and skating aids at half off the regular price!

Help for Our Youngest Skaters

Our Family Skate is great for our newest skaters! We have Zippy Adjustable Skates, which go over the shoe, have a lower and wider wheel base, and roll more slowly. These are great for learning balance. We also rent Skate Mates for skaters aged 10 and under for $2.50 which is 1/2 off the regular price.

Discounted Admission for All

As families grow so do the expenses to go out and have fun together. We want to help and so during our Family Skate you can enjoy a lower admission at just $6 per skater. Don’t have your own skates? No problem! Rent your choice of inline or roller skates for just $4.00.

Themed Skate Sessions

Our Family Skate is a great session to host themed skates throughout the year. Whether celebrating a holiday or creating our own fun with a Superhero Skate, these can feature costumes, festivities and prizes, and themed music! Themed events may have special pricing on Admission.

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

❤️

Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

Blackout Skate

For a portion of the session, we will black out the rink and side aisle lighting. While there is still enough visibility to navigate the skating floor, the darker environment creates a concert-style atmosphere. event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

❤️

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

Hosted by Swamp Witch Tabletop at Front Street Taproom

 First Wednesday of Every Month
 6:30 PM – 9:30 PM

Ever wanted to try Dungeons & Dragons but weren’t sure where to start? Join us for an evening of storytelling, adventure, and tabletop fun in a welcoming space for women and femme-presenting players.

 Beginner-friendly
 No experience required
 Pre-made Level 3 characters provided
 D&D 2024 ruleset with a little homebrew magic
 “D&D Light” character options available for new players
 Meet fellow gamers and make new friends

Hosted on the Mezzanine at Front Street Taproom
614 Main Ave | Downtown Fargo

Hosted by Valley Vital Medicine
First Friday of Every Month | 3–6 PM
Location: Valley Vital Medicine, Fargo, ND

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

❤️

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

This nighttime session brings a great atmosphere with good music to skate to, games, a blackout skate and glow sticks! Every paid skater gets a FREE GLOW STICK!

Blackout Skate

For a portion of the session, we will black out the rink and side aisle lighting. While there is still enough visibility to navigate the skating floor, the darker environment creates a concert-style atmosphere. Glow Sticks

We pick great music for dancing and skating for this Friday night session. Nothing pairs with specialty lights and blackout skates like songs with a good rhythm!

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Catering to families with young skaters, this Saturday morning session offers discounted admission for families along with age-appropriate music and skating aids at half off the regular price!

Help for Our Youngest Skaters

Our Family Skate is great for our newest skaters! We have Zippy Adjustable Skates, which go over the shoe, have a lower and wider wheel base, and roll more slowly. These are great for learning balance. We also rent Skate Mates for skaters aged 10 and under for $2.50 which is 1/2 off the regular price.

Discounted Admission for All

As families grow so do the expenses to go out and have fun together. We want to help and so during our Family Skate you can enjoy a lower admission at just $6 per skater. Don’t have your own skates? No problem! Rent your choice of inline or roller skates for just $4.00.

Themed Skate Sessions

Our Family Skate is a great session to host themed skates throughout the year. Whether celebrating a holiday or creating our own fun with a Superhero Skate, these can feature costumes, festivities and prizes, and themed music! Themed events may have special pricing on Admission.

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Healing Harvest Market

Hosted by Valley Vital Medicine
First Friday of Every Month | 3–6 PM
Location: Valley Vital Medicine, Fargo, ND
Website: https://valleyvitalmedicine.com

The Healing Harvest Market is a monthly community gathering focused on faith, health, and local nourishment. Each market features local farmers, artisans, and wellness-focused businesses offering clean food, handcrafted goods, and natural wellness resources.

This event is an opportunity for the community to come together, support small local producers, and learn more about healthy, intentional living. The market also highlights ways to support local families and individuals facing health challenges.

All are welcome to attend and connect with others who value community wellness, local agriculture, and meaningful living.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

Catering to families and skaters of all ages and skill levels. Join us for a midweek session with discounted admission! Just $6 per skater, plus $4.00 skate rental if needed.

Family Night Out

Discount Night is a great way to get some midweek fun for the whole family at a great rate. Bring friends and extended family for good music, games and food!

Groups & Clubs

Whether you’re in a college club, book club or sports team, our group rates can’t be beaten! Reserve your group of 15 or more skaters at get admission for $6 per skater, which includes choice of rental!

Daycares & Youth Groups

Skating is a great way to get your daycare or youth group out for a night of fun! This midweek session is a great opportunity. Reserve a group of 15 or more and get our group rates – just $6 per skater, which includes choice of skate rental! Groups also get our meal deal (hotdogs, chips, and small drink) for just $5 per skater.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

❤️

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

❤️

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Healing Harvest Market

Hosted by Valley Vital Medicine
First Friday of Every Month | 3–6 PM
Location: Valley Vital Medicine, Fargo, ND
Website: https://valleyvitalmedicine.com

The Healing Harvest Market is a monthly community gathering focused on faith, health, and local nourishment. Each market features local farmers, artisans, and wellness-focused businesses offering clean food, handcrafted goods, and natural wellness resources.

This event is an opportunity for the community to come together, support small local producers, and learn more about healthy, intentional living. The market also highlights ways to support local families and individuals facing health challenges.

All are welcome to attend and connect with others who value community wellness, local agriculture, and meaningful living.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

Help for Our Youngest Skaters

Our Family Skate is great for our newest skaters! We have Zippy Adjustable Skates, which go over the shoe, have a lower and wider wheel base, and roll more slowly. event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

❤️

event.description:
Meet up and chat with others with similar interests. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Refreshments will be provided.

Check the calendar for updates – https://larl.org/mondaymeetup/

First Monday of the Month – Craft Connection

Join us to get cozy, craft and chat! This is an opportunity to leave distractions behind and focus on your craft. Bring whatever project you are working on and meet up with other local crafters. You can share your expertise, learn from others or just enjoy some distraction-free time to yourself. Refreshments will be provided.

Second Monday of the Month – Best Sellers Book Club

Join the Moorhead Public Library’s Best Sellers Book Club and see what the buzz is about in the latest popular books!

Third Monday of the Month – Game Night

Join us to get cozy, play games, and chat! This is an opportunity to meet up with others who enjoy playing games. Come with friends, or make some new ones! Bring your favorite card or board game, or try one of ours! Refreshments will be provided.

Fourth Monday of the Month – Silent Reading Club

Join us at the Moorhead Library for quiet, sustained reading at our new Silent Book Club! All readers are welcome—ebooks or audiobooks, poetry or prose, fiction or non-fiction… it’s BYOBook. The library will provide comfortable seating and light refreshments.

Fifth Monday of the Month – Guided Activity

Join us each month for different activities lead by experts in their respective disciplines. Any needed supplies will be provided.

event.description:
Safe Harbor is a small, in-person, facilitated community peer-support and emotional processing group set up to offer more human connection.

The group will run in 4-week closed cycles, with up to 10 members each cycle, and will be meeting for about 90 minutes on the weekend. This is a non-therapy, community-based space, and it is not a substitute for therapy or crisis services.

Safe Harbor may be a good fit for people experiencing grief, transition, relational stress, feeling overwhelmed, or just wanting a place to process life with others humans.

Please note, this group is not a fit for anyone in immediate crisis. If you need urgent support, please call or text 988.

If you are interested, you can learn more about the group, facilitator, and also complete a quick interest form at safeharborfm.org

Help for Our Youngest Skaters

Our Family Skate is great for our newest skaters! We have Zippy Adjustable Skates, which go over the shoe, have a lower and wider wheel base, and roll more slowly. event.description:
As America’s premier John Denver tribute artist, Ted Vigil has wowed sellout crowds from coast to coast. He embodies the late great music icon in look as well as voice with an unforgettable performance. He was invited to perform as the John Denver tribute artist at John Denver’s “Windstar Foundation” in Aspen, Colorado. John Denver’s lead guitarist, Steve Weisberg, performed with Ted and described his performance as “uncanny”.

For this wonderful and exciting performance, expect to hear John Denver’s most beloved hits, like ‘Take Me Home Country Roads”, “Leaving on a Jet Plane”, “Annie’s Song”. “Rocky Mountain High”, “Sunshine On My Shoulder”, ‘Thank God I’m a Country Boy” and many more. If you are A John Denver fan you definitely will not want to miss this performance.

There are a limited number of VIP 1 seats available to this event. They include best in house seating in the first three rows, meet & greet with the artist and a photo opportunity. Also, includes a free glass of wine and a fantastic piece of cheesecake from Indulge Artisan Cheesecake in Medford.

Celebrated for its campy, outrageous style and inclusive, gender-bending themes, Rocky Horror follows newlyweds Brad and Janet, who stumble into the castle of the mad-scientist alien, Dr. Frank-N-Furter—where their innocence quickly unravels. The longest-running theatrical release in history, it’s a deliciously bizarre cult phenomenon that practically begs for audience participation.

The Rocky Horror Experience

* The Rocky Horror Tour & The Craterian Theater want to make sure that everyone has a great time at the RHPS.

The idea behind Rocky Horror’s traditions—shouting callback lines, throwing props, and dressing up is to have FUN, not to be destructive to the venue or disruptive to fellow fans. Every venue and every Rocky Horror experience is unique. The following guidelines will help you and other members of the audience enjoy this special night at the Craterian. Please ensure that you are conscious of those around you and respectful of theater staff and volunteers. 

  • You CAN use props, but only when indicated during the show.
  • You CAN purchase a prop bag in the theater lobby prior to the show ($5). No additional props (beyond what is in the bag provided by the Rocky Horror Tour) are allowed into the theater. 
  • You CAN yell, but remember everyone wants to hear and see the movie, so please keep yelling to the appropriate moments.
  • You CAN (and should) dress up. We’ll be giving out prizes for our Rocky Horror Costume Contest!

event.description:
Youth Symphony of Southern Oregon
Fall Concert Series Performance
November 14, 2026, 7:30 p.m.

The Youth Symphony of Southern Oregon (YSSO) will present a performance at the Collier Center’s Craterian Theater at 7:30PM on Saturday, November 14, 2026. The concert will showcase the musicians of the Youth Symphony and the Youth Orchestra under the direction of interim conductor Steve Kessler.

The featured Youth Symphony work on the Fall Concert Series program will be the Finale of Max Bruch’s Violin Concerto No. 1 in G minor, Op. 26. The violin soloist will be 2026 Concerto Competition winner Louvencia Blumhardt. The concert will also include music by Antonin Dvořák, Brian Balmages, Paul Dukas, Nicolai Rimsky-Korsakov, and others.

Since 1988, the Youth Symphony of Southern Oregon has brought accomplished young musicians to the Craterian Theater and stages across the Rogue Valley, performing orchestral masterworks, concerti, film, ballet, and opera scores, and contemporary music. YSSO performances are accessible, audiences are multigenerational, and the impact of the inspiring performances is lasting.

The YSSO believes music is a catalyst for community engagement, personal growth, and a cohesive society. The YSSO supplements school music programs, strengthens the region’s arts sector, and gives young people a place where their contribution genuinely matters. In addition to the performances, the musicians build listening skills, empathy, lasting friendships, and the discipline that comes from mastering intellectual and technical challenges. Whether a YSSO musician goes on to become an engineer, educator, nurse, physician, business or faith leader, parent, professional
musician, attorney, accountant, or astronaut, the habits of collaboration travel with them.

The Youth Symphony of Southern Oregon is an organization in which every person’s sound contributes to the music.

With warmth and humor, he and a dazzling tribe of world-class performers carry audiences back in time to a wintry night in an Irish “rambling house,” where traditional song, dance, music, and stories bring a community together for one wondrous evening. You don’t have to be Irish to appreciate this moving and intimate show that reminds us all of the power and joy of the ancient art of storytelling. Get your tickets early to this holiday treasure.

event.description:
Dr. Seuss’s The Cat in the Hat Live on Stage

event.description:
A spectacular World Premiere production, Alice in Wonderland reimagines Lewis Carroll’s beloved story through a bold, wildly imaginative artistic vision – featuring breathtaking sets and costumes designed in collaboration with world-renowned artist Romero Britto. This one-of-a- kind production pushes the boundaries of classical ballet, blending the elegance of a world- class cast with the visual spectacle of Broadway-style theatrical design, and the vibrant energy of pop art. The result is a new form of live entertainment that amazes, surprises, and transports audiences into a world unlike anything they’ve seen on stage.

Step into a magical world where imagination comes alive. Audiences follow Alice down the rabbit hole into a surreal wonderland bursting with color, fantasy, and theatrical charm – from a charming Mad Hatter to a delightfully parodic Queen of Hearts. Each scene explodes with immersive visuals, extraordinary characters, and the grace and power of an international cast of ballet stars representing leading ballet traditions from around the world, including Spain, Brazil, Poland, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, Italy, Austria, Georgia, Iceland, Japan, Moldova, Romania, Belarus, Armenia, Mongolia, and Albania.

With its sophisticated storytelling, bold visual design, and captivating performances, Alice in Wonderland enchants children and adults alike.

Suggested for Audiences ages 3 and over

event.description:
The Peacherine Ragtime Society Orchestra: Stage & Sound Spectacular featuring “The General”

Under the direction of virtuoso Andrew Greene, The Peacherine Ragtime Society Orchestra (PRSO) is the leading professional ragtime orchestra in the United States, known for reviving the syncopated stylings of the early 1900s through ragtime, marches, and theater music. For this special performance, the 12-piece ensemble performs a live, reconstructed orchestral score to Buster Keaton’s 1926 silent film, The General—widely regarded as one of the greatest films ever made—providing an authentic, energetic sound-track that perfectly matches the film’s action.

event.description:
Join us for a fun (and FREE) Mixer Tournament the 1st Monday of every month @ 6:40pm. This is a great tournament for people of all skill levels that want to play with new people in a more relaxed competitive environment.

Join our Discord server to engage with our community & register for tournaments online:
https://discord.gg/dnqG5wNzSa

CODE OF CONDUCT:
Please review our community Code of Conduct before attending, as ALL attendees will be responsible for upholding this during the tournament:
https://bit.ly/KQPDXcoc
We will have extra masks on hand if needed.

⏰ Schedule:
5 PM – 6:05 PM: Sign ups!
6:05 PM – 6:40 PM: Draft picks & warmup games
6:40 PM – 10 PM (ish): Mixer Tournament games

🕹 Format:
Exact format depends on the number of teams that sign up, and will be announced the night-of. Occasionally we’ll swap this out for other fun and unique formats. That said, here’s what we usually do:
<= 4 teams: Round Robin -> Ladder
5-6 teams: Round Robin
7+ teams: Double Elim
You don’t need to find or bring a team with you! All skill levels encouraged to sign up – including if you’ve never played before. You’ll sign up individually for the tournament (BEFORE 6:05pm!) at the venue, and we’ll find a few people that want to captain. After sign ups close, we’ll be doing a snake draft where captains choose members for their team. Please stay in the area between 6 – 6:30pm so we can find you after the draft is complete and get started on time!
If you show up late for signups there’s ~no guarantee~ you’ll get to play in the tournament. Please keep that in mind! If you’re running late but you know you’ll be there BEFORE 6:30pm, please message someone attending and ask if there are any options.

🏆 Prizes:
1st🥇: $50 gift certificate for the team to split & $10 game cards for each player.
2nd🥈: $50 gift certificate for the team to split.
3rd🥉: $25 gift certificate for the team to split.

🎥 Stream & Bracket:
You’ll be able to see the Twitch stream, Twitch chat, and the Challonge bracket on the Live Matches page of our website here:
https://killerqueenpdx.buzz/live
If you’d prefer direct links, we’ll be streaming the tournament on our Twitch page here:
https://www.twitch.tv/kqpdx
The Challonge bracket will be posted here:
https://challonge.com/communities/kqpdx

↩️ Finding the KQ cabinets:
🔵 Blue Side 🔵
Once you enter Ground Kontrol you’ll need to walk straight back and around the first bar, take a left and go all the way to the back room. Killer Queen is in the back-right corner of the blue room, near the second bar.

The goal is to keep BSSC a casual space that boosts new players and further helps build the community. Getting wrecked constantly can be exhausting and discouraging. So the difference with BSSC and other tournaments is the introduction of a handicap system. Inspired by bowling leagues and golf tournaments to help even the playing field and make it more fair. The format will be 4 games of a matchplay format with a one game final for the top 4.

Handicaps will be determined by player ratings in MatchPlay. Handicaps will be a percentage taken off of your score at the end of the game.

Expert: 40% off
A: 30% off
B: 15% off
C: 0% off
D, E and unrated: 0% off and can play one extra ball

Example with a score of 1,304, 216,800 this is what would count
Expert: 782,530,080 (1,304, 216,800 × 0.6)
A: 912,951,760 (1,304, 216,800 x 0.7)
B: 1,108,584,280 (1,304,216,800 x 0.85)
C: 1,304,216,800
D, E and unrated: 1,304,216,800 (plus an extra ball)

Sometimes an experimental format may happen!

event.description:
Weekend workshop: Oct 31, Nov 1

9-4pm

Topics covered:

• Painting Demonstration – 4 oil painting guidelines
• Simplifying with parent colors
• Color mixing
• Big brush advantage
• Straightforward compositions
• Importances of Edges
• Creating depth in your painting

Oil Painting – Paul Gallo 717-608-7190

Supplies can be bought locally at Michaels or on-line at Dick Blick or Cheap Joes.

 

BASIC OIL PAINT COLORS: Ultramarine Blue, Cadmium Yellow Medium, Cadmium Red, Alizarin Crimson Permanent, Burnt Sienna and Titanium White

 

PAINT BRANDS: 

Recommended Professional Brands: Windsor Newton or Gamblin  

Less Expensive Recommended Brands: Gamblin 1980, WindsorNewton “Winton”, or Utrecht

Michaels, Dick Blick and Cheap Joes usually have 9-color paint sets for about $45 which will work fine.

I don’t recommend using the cheapest student grade paints.

 

PAPER TOWELS – 1 roll of paper towels

BRUSHES:

Brushes come in three basic shapes – rounds, brights, flats and filberts.  Rounds are long and tubular, like a watercolor brush.  Brights and flats are flat and square, with brights being short and flats being long. Fiberts combine the advantage of flats but creating the softer paint edge of a round. I use mostly brights, flats and filberts, but each type of brush gives you a unique mark.

Bring whatever brushes you have but it would good to have these four.

Round: #6 or #8

Large flat or bright; about ¾” to 1” wide

Smaller flat or bright; about 1/4” wide

Bring whatever brushes you have and feel comfortable with.

PALETTE:

Disposal palette paper or Plastic sealable palette

 

PALETTE KNIFE:

Metal palette knife, size about 4” in length. (For color mixing,scraping paint, laying-in bold color and cleaning the palette.)

SOLVENT/ AND CONTAINERS:

Turpenoid (odorless substitute for turpentine) and a container to hold Turpenoid. (Tuna cans work well)

Water container for acrylic.

CANVAS OR ART BOARDS:

Two stretched canvas, canvas board or Masonite. Common sizes9x12” or 11×14”.

Please bring good reference photos to paint from. Photos on your phone are too small, so get a good photo print of any phone photos you want to use.  Photos reference on your iPad and laptop are large enough to use. Here are two free resources that offer artists good photo reference.

This monthly reading series is intended to prioritize the safety, creativity, and stories of Black people, Indigenous people, and People of Color.

Come listen to our featured readers, or sign up to share your work in our open mic. Readings will be followed by a short community discussion. Hosted by Kyle Yoshioka and Jessica Meza-Torres. The featured reader for September is Diego Sanchez.

This event is open to everyone, but only people who identify as Black, Indigenous, and/or People of Color will be invited to read. If you have any questions, please contact Jessica Meza-Torres at jmezatorres24@gmail.com or Kyle Yoshioka at kyle.yoshioka@gmail.com.

event.description:
Does what you write or how you write it change with the seasons? In these quarterly gatherings we’ll meet to be inspired by the turn of the world. From autumn leaves to springtime flowers, rain and snow and sun, we’ll consider nature’s shifts and how we can incorporate them into our writing practice. We’ll also reflect on the impact of climate change on our seasonal rhythms and on our writing. Through brief readings, writing prompts, and generative exercises, we’ll welcome in and attune our writing to the time of year.

Access Program
We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available.

Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.

Liaison position
Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts.

Apply here for the liaison position.

event.description:
In this 8 week, Wednesday morning class, we will read, explore and discuss the sequential poem in contemporary American poetry, from poets such as Lucille Clifton and Robert Hass to Sherwin Bitsui and Nam Le, and many more besides.

What makes a sequential poem work? How does a constellation of poems react to and inform each other? What can be included in a poem? What are the boundaries of a sequence? We’ll address questions such as these, and others, as we dive into this unique and exhilarating form.

Alongside scintillating conversations about published poetry we will build our own “mixtape” poems through a series of fun and inspiring exercises. Each participant will leave with a deepened and strengthened relationship to poetry as well as two publishable poetic sequences of their own.

Access Program
We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available.

Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.

Mitchell S. Jackson is the winner of the 2021 Pulitzer Prize in Feature Writing and the 2021 National Magazine Award in Feature Writing. Jackson’s debut novel, The Residue Years, won a Whiting Award and the Ernest J. Gaines Award for Literary Excellence. His essay collection Survival Math was named a best book of 2019 by fifteen publications. Jackson’s other honors include fellowships, grants, and awards from the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation, Creative Capital, the Cullman Center of the New York Public Library, the Lannan Foundation, PEN America, and TED. His writing has been featured on the cover of the New York Times Magazine, the New York Times Book Review, Time, and Esquire, as well as in The New Yorker, Harper’s Magazine, the Paris Review, the Guardian, and elsewhere. Jackson is a contributing writer for the New York Times Magazine and a columnist for Esquire. He holds the John O. event.description:
Literary Arts and The Reser are thrilled to present Min Jin Lee, author of the beloved novels Pachinko (an international bestseller and National Book Award finalist) and Free Food for Millionaires, for a conversation about her new book, American Hagwon.  

 American Hagwon is both “a classic in the making and a novel distinctly of our moment, one that helps us find firmer ground in a world unmoored from a most basic concern: how do we care for one another?” 

Min Jin Lee will be joined in conversation by Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and author Mitchell S. Jackson.

About the book:

In schools and churches, hotel rooms and nail salons, law firms and fried-fish shops; in cramped, dingy apartments and luxury, gated communities, the men, women, and children in American Hagwon struggle to find satisfaction and meaning in a world that seems to grow less forgiving with each passing year. Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children—Bo, DH, and Mido—find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John’s oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis.

Desperately striving to regain their footing, they leave Seoul for Sydney and eventually settle in Southern California—where new vistas of opportunity open up for the children as their parents, strangers in a strange land, must adjust to a new life in which their experience and education mean little, and they set their sights on whatever it takes to provide for their children’s futures. The Kohs, their friends, relatives, and even their foes move in and out of each other’s lives as they navigate new courses across the years, always nursing the almost all-consuming faith that education will lead the next generation to success and security.

In American Hagwon, Min Jin Lee has crafted an unforgettable, panoramic novel where the smallest of gestures can have enormous repercussions, where the bonds of family and of memory twist and fray but rarely break, and where willful self-sacrifice—for the benefit of loved ones and even strangers—is a kind of prayer.

event.description:
What about any story makes you want to keep reading? In this class, we’ll look at the openings of several short stories and creative nonfiction pieces with a special focus on the craft: how was the story written in a way that makes it successful? What aspects might make a reader (and editor) keep reading?

We’ll borrow themes and ideas from those stories for in our in-class writing exercises. We’ll read amazing, inspiring work from Lauren Groff, Flannery O’Connor, Ling Ma, and others.

Every class session will include:

● A detailed, guided warm up
● In-class story dissection
● Suggested at-home reading and writing exercises

Each writer will have the opportunity to workshop the opening page of a story two times.

Access Program
We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available.

Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.

Liaison position
Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts.

Apply here for the liaison position.

event.description:
Literary Arts is excited to welcome author and journalist Ali Francis to celebrate her debut book, The Curious Lives of Vegetables, a wild journey through the hidden histories of plants.

Francis will be joined by Portland writers Lola Milholland (Group Living and Other Recipes) and Andrew Barton (Free Food: earth eating, The Long Loaf, The Myrtlewood Cookbook) for a conversation moderated by environmental journalist and author Devon Fredericksen (How to Camp in the Woods).

Together, they’ll explore what food can tell us about how we live: our relationships with plants and place, the ways knowledge and traditions move between people, what gets lost when food systems become less diverse, and what we might recover by paying closer attention to the things we eat. Moving from vegetables and biodiversity to bread, communal tables, regional foodways, and the everyday work of feeding people, the conversation will consider food not simply as something we consume, but as a reflection of our relationships with the natural world.

About the book:

Why are some carrots purple? What does a 1,000-year-old lotus seed have to tell us about survival? How did a tomato named for Paul Robeson become a political symbol? And what disappears when a vegetable disappears?

In The Curious Lives of Vegetables, Australian journalist Ali Francis goes digging into the astonishing stories hiding in our crisper drawers, gardens, markets, and seed banks. Across more than 100 beautifully illustrated stories, she traces the plants we eat through migration and colonialism, politics and religion, extinction and revival, revealing vegetables as living records of human history — and essential seeds for a more resilient future. 

Along the way, Francis encounters ancient seeds brought back from the dead, vegetables carried across borders by displaced communities, plants transformed by centuries of human preference, and varieties now teetering on the edge of extinction. At once playful, deeply researched, and urgent, The Curious Lives of Vegetables asks us to look again at the ordinary plants on our plates, and to consider their extraordinary importance.

event.description:
The spiral holds great meaning for cultures all over the world and has captivated our attention throughout ancient and modern time. Whether of metaphysical and philosophical significance, or the many scientific and biological iterations of this powerful symbol, the multi-faceted spiral will be our muse.

In this 3-part generative writing workshop, we’ll expand our writing across multiple genres including poetry, essay, and narrative with prompts inspired by multicultural authors. Thematically, we’ll move through Irish-Celtic mysticism, spiraling seasons of emergence, Afro-futurist science fiction, and our personal place within the great spiral. We’ll engage impactful elements of style and craft from our mentor texts like punctuation, dialogue, and symbol to enhance writing of resonance. Some time will be devoted to giving and receiving feedback as well as sharing in a supportive space. Writers of all levels and backgrounds are welcome.

Course Outcomes
Writers will:
Explore a variety of multicultural texts as inspiration for writing.
Draft poems, creative non-fiction, and narrative pieces related to spirals.
Engage elements of craft and style from multigenre model texts.
Enhance writing through feedback and sharing in positive and supportive circles.

Access Program
We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available.

Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.

Liaison position
Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts.

Apply here for the liaison position.

event.description:
The Literary Arts Bookstore & Cafe is excited to welcome author Kelly Grace Thomas to celebrate the release of her memoir-in-verse, Future Tense. Thomas will be joined in conversation by local poet Joy Sullivan.

About the book:

Reckoning with infertility, adoption, and love under pressure, Kelly Grace Thomas’s Future Tense is a searing memoir-in-verse about a woman’s fight to become a mother while losing her own. 

Thomas spends three years trying for a child who never arrives. As she struggles with infertility, her mother is dying of Stage IV uterine cancer, and the desire for a child turns urgent—a countdown. As her mother’s health deteriorates, time narrows, pressure builds, and the clock refuses to slow. As her marriage strains and the world remakes itself without her, Thomas refuses to give up. The fertility clinic is the coldest place on earth; still, she keeps going—through years of medical gaslighting, IVF consults, mounting debt, and backhanded blame—finally welcoming her daughter through adoption just months before her mother’s death.

Intimate and unflinching, Future Tense interrogates the intertwined joys and griefs of womanhood and motherhood—and how biology can sometimes turn against us. Thomas approaches illness and loss with clarity and care, writing with a generosity that welcomes readers in. Despite their brevity, these poems refuse despair, finding meaning and connection even in the hardest seasons of life.

In Dear Blind Lady, Deafblind author and disability rights activist Elsa Sjunneson delivers candid, funny, and practical guidance in an advice-column format. Written for disabled readers, allies, friends, family members, coworkers, and anyone who wants to build a more accessible and respectful world, this book tackles the questions nondisabled people may be afraid to ask—and disabled people are tired of answering.

event.description:
Join us at The Literary Arts Bookstore & Cafe for an evening of readings featuring members of the American Literary Translators Association’s BIPOC Translators Caucus. Co-organized by Elete Nelson-Fearon and Jon Cho-Polizzi, this year’s BIPOC Caucus Reading features translations from Arabic, Chinese, German, Korean, Spanish, and more!

In addition to readings by the co-hosts, featured translators include: Stine An, Kareem Abu-Zeid, Chenxin Jiang, and Noelle de la Paz.

The event is free to attend and open to all.

event.description:
Literary Arts is thrilled to partner with our neighbor, SCRAP PDX, for a special crafty event!

Join us in celebrating the return of the crows! You may have followed crows all around Portland for the upcoming Wildwood film. Now it’s your turn to create your own crow with SCRAP!

Hand-sew small plush treasure crows! 🐦‍⬛ Crows love shiny things, so be sure to decorate them with sequins, beads, and trinkets. Bring a friend! Make a friend! Grab a beverage, browse the books, and gather round to hand-sew some mystical, magical bird plush!

Traceable templates & embroidery stitch printouts provided. Self-guided & beginner-friendly. A SCRAP educator will be ready to assist newer sewists with hand-sewing basics!

This is a ticketed event. Drop-ins welcome. Get tickets here.

event.description:
Writing animals in fiction is a complex, rewarding and rejuvenating process. From “Animal Farm” to “Mink River”, several authors have gravitated to the form to deepen empathy in the reader and establish an immersive fictional world. In this six week class, students will work on several in-class writing prompts to develop both writing and research skills to render an animal presence precisely on the page.

Students will receive a detailed booklist with resources and students can plan to complete 8-10 pages of a fictional story draft before the end of the class. An individual office hours meeting with the instructor is also included in the class description. Ideal class for beginning and advanced writers alike.

Access Program
We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available.

Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.

event.description:
Join us at The Literary Arts Bookstore & Cafe for a spooky storytelling open mic.

Readers will have five minutes to enchant us with their ghoulish tales! Our only requirement is that these stories are true—or at least, true to you. Audience members will vote to decide who wins the title of Ghost King and brings home a special prize!

Each story should take five minutes or less to tell. Spots are limited; names will be drawn from a fishbowl.

You may bring notes to read from, but we encourage free-flow oral storytelling.

event.description:
When Henry James came to write his short classic book on his predecessor Nathaniel Hawthorne (who was an important influence on James), he wrote, with tongue in cheek, a description of the cultural and social wasteland that an ambitious American writer faced in Hawthorne’s day in finding material for fiction:

No sovereign, no court,…no aristocracy, no church,…no army, no diplomatic service, no country gentlemen, no palaces, no castles, nor manors, nor old country-houses, nor parsonages, nor thatched cottages nor ivied ruins; no cathedrals, nor abbeys, nor little Norman churches; no great Universities nor public schools; no literature, no novels, no museums, no pictures, no political society, no sporting class…. Some such list as that might be drawn up of the absent things in American life, the effect of which,…upon an English or a French imagination, would probably as a general thing be appalling.

And yet Hawthorne, as James well knew, in his most memorable works created a brilliant array of imaginative fictions drawn from the riches of New England life—its legends, tall tales, landscapes, and history. Rather than being appalled, Hawthorne, as James well knew, in his most memorable works created a brilliant array of imaginative fictions drawn from the riches of New England life—its legends, tall tales, landscapes, and history

This Delve seminar will focus on Hawthorne’s short stories—among the most thrilling, strange, and memorable in the American canon. We will explore his first collection of stories, Twice-Told Tales (1837, 1851) as well as a small selection of extraordinary later stories.

Hawthorne worked his American materials in a diverse range of genres—horror, the gothic, romance, the fantastic, moral tales, allegory—and narrative subjects—ambiguities of love and loss, gender and sex, guilt, conflicts between authority and non-conformists, secrets, science and magic, modernity and tradition, past and present, shadows, and a repudiation of tyranny.

What marks all the works we will delve into during this seminar is mystery, ambiguity, thrills and chills, and a keen sense of the ways in which power seeks to dominate the individual. These characteristics alone make him our contemporary.

Writer and Hawthorne fan Rosemary Mahoney writes:

Whatever form they take, Twice-Told Tales, like salt and sugar on daily staples, are a kind of splendid seasoning, coaxing into acuteness the full, strange flavor of life…. Sit this evening by your brownest lamp and read these stories. If you find yourself unstirred, unengaged, un-creeped, then perhaps—and I propose this in the politest way possible—you should check your pulse.

Texts:
We will use the Modern Library Classics edition of Twice-Told Tales, with an introduction by Mahoney, plus a few stories from his other collections of short stories to be supplied in pdf. These will include the proto-feminist male-gaze horror story “The Birthmark.”

Access Program
We want our writing classes and seminars to be accessible to everyone, regardless of income and background. We understand that our tuition structure can present obstacles for some people. Our Access Program offers writing class and seminar tuitions at a reduced rate. Most writing classes have at least one access spot available.

Please apply here for access rate tuition. Contact Susan Moore at susan@literary-arts.org if you have questions.

Liaison position
Every in-person class and seminar at Literary Arts has one liaison position. Liaisons perform specific duties for each class meeting. If you are a liaison for a class or seminar, the full amount of your tuition is covered by Literary Arts.

Apply here for the liaison position.

event.description:
This monthly reading series is intended to prioritize the safety, creativity, and stories of Black people, Indigenous people, and People of Color.

Come listen to our featured readers, or sign up to share your work in our open mic. Readings will be followed by a short community discussion. Hosted by Kyle Yoshioka and Jessica Meza-Torres. The featured reader for October will be announced soon.

This event is open to everyone, but only people who identify as Black, Indigenous, and/or People of Color will be invited to read. If you have any questions, please contact Jessica Meza-Torres at jmezatorres24@gmail.com or Kyle Yoshioka at kyle.yoshioka@gmail.com.
